rule_name: Use Past Perfect for Action Before the Narrative Present
quote: All seven sat the same examination
why: the chapter's narration is present tense and this refers to something that finished before the current scene, so simple past collapses the two time frames together instead of signaling it happened earlier
suggestion: All seven had sat the same examination

why: the sentence is already complete and correct before this final comma, and the tail only tells the reader how to take the quoting that the previous sentence already framed as part of an argument
suggestion: Ruth quotes the sentencing ranges from memory, twice, at Eli.

quote: what it never touches, what it does if it's noticed, and what happens if any one of the seven says stop
why: three parallel 'what' clauses in a row is the anaphoric three-beat list the automatic-fail table says to collapse, regardless of how fast the pacing reads
suggestion: collapse to one line, e.g. "nine pages covering what it never touches, what happens if it's noticed, and how fast it stops if any one of the seven says so"

quote: she is aware of that the entire time she is writing them
why: this states the fact of her awareness as a summary instead of rendering the texture of holding the clearance and the nine pages in her head at once
suggestion: and the badge is still clipped to her bag on the desk while she types the ninth page

quote: and she is aware of that the entire time she is writing them, and she does not stop
why: an internal state and a decisive final action are given identical grammatical weight by the flat and...and chain, erasing the escalation between them
suggestion: aware of it the entire time she is writing them, she does not stop
